title: Active users by signup date
statement_markdown: Return id and name for active users who signed up on or after 2026-01-01. Sort by id.

examples.explanation: This output comes from the visible sample data.

starter_query:
SELECT id, name
FROM users
WHERE
hints: Both the activity flag and signup date belong in WHERE.
Compare the date with a PostgreSQL DATE literal and combine conditions with AND.
explanation: WHERE removes rows that fail either condition before SELECT returns id and name. ORDER BY makes the result deterministic. A common mistake is using OR, which includes inactive or old users. A composite index may help when this filter is common.
reference_solution: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE active = true AND signup_date >= DATE '2026-01-01' ORDER BY id;
complexity: A table scan without an index; appropriate indexes can reduce examined rows.

validation.setup_sql: CREATE TABLE users(id integer primary key,name text,active boolean,signup_date date); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Ada',true,'2026-01-04'),(2,'Bob',false,'2026-02-01'),(3,'Lin',true,'2025-12-31'),(4,'Maya',true,'2026-03-10');
